- If sentiment is positive and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots; model tends to overreact to sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming; model often underestimates downside risk.
- After a sharp price spike, model overestimates continuation; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to prevent over-optimism.
- When sentiment is flat (0.00) and forecast is trending upward, reduce slope; mean reversion is likely in flat sentiment periods.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a high, model often fails to anticipate reversal; adjust forecast downward by 5–10% in first 5 days post-spike.
- In low-sentiment periods, model tends to overforecast mean; apply a downward bias of 2–5% to forecast mean if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
